evidence.note: Garbačiauskas explicitly treats Definitions as pseudo-Platonic and a late interpolation reflecting later philosophical traditions.
Benati's critical-edition research project is explicitly devoted to the Pseudo-Platonic Definitions and treats the collection as chronologically stratified.

rationale: Definitions is not regarded as a work of Plato in modern scholarship. Garbačiauskas characterizes it as a pseudo-Platonic late interpolation whose vocabulary reflects several later philosophical strata, including early Stoicism; current critical work likewise treats the text explicitly as the pseudo-Platonic Definitions. D is appropriate because Platonic authorship is not a live modern position, while the collection remains historically important to the wider Platonic corpus.
